analyst_view.overall: Early view: a bottom-four clash in all but name. United are 18th with no league win since August and play Sporting in the Champions League on 25 November, while Coventry are 17th, a point above them, and lost 3-1 at Everton. United's defence concedes heavily, but they also scored four against Villa, so this could be open.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: United's defence has conceded more than any side in Europe's top five leagues in all competitions, they just drew 4-4 with Villa, and Coventry scored first at Everton. United must chase the win at home, which leaves gaps.

corners.text: The site has 8.9 corners. I lean higher: United will push hard at home with Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo wide, and Coventry will defend deep for long spells. More corners for United than the 5.6 suggested.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. I lean higher: this is a near-relegation clash with both sides desperate, and Frank Lampard was angry with the officials after the Everton game. Three cards seems low for that kind of tension.

shots.text: The site has 31.8 shots, 22.2 for United. I lean lower: United are without Benjamin Sesko, probably Marcus Rashford, and Carlos Baleba, which takes punch out of their attack. Plenty of shots, but not over 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I agree: fewer United shots than the model expects, but an open game with poor defending on both sides should still give both goalkeepers a lot to do.
